related_questions.question: Why am I having a psoriasis flare-up?

text_blocks.snippet: Psoriasis flare-ups are often triggered by a combination of factors, including your immune system's response, genetics, and environmental triggers. These triggers can include skin injuries, infections, stress, certain medications, and even weather conditions. Understanding these triggers and taking steps to manage them can help reduce the frequency and severity of flare-ups.
snippet_highlighted_words: often triggered by a combination of factors, including your immune system's response, genetics, and environmental triggers

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the reasons behind psoriasis flare-ups:

list.snippet: Psoriasis is an autoimmune disease where the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy skin cells.
This leads to an accelerated skin cell growth cycle, where new skin cells are produced too quickly and don't have enough time to mature before being shed.
This rapid turnover results in the buildup of skin cells on the surface, causing the characteristic red, scaly patches of psoriasis.
Psoriasis tends to run in families, suggesting a genetic component.
Certain genes, like the HLA-Cw6 allele, have been identified as risk factors for developing psoriasis.

list.title: Skin Injuries:
list.snippet: Cuts, scrapes, sunburns, or even tattoos can trigger a flare-up in susceptible individuals, a phenomenon known as the Koebner response.

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: Strep throat, skin infections, and other infections can sometimes precede a psoriasis flare-up.

list.title: Stress:
list.snippet: Emotional stress can activate the immune system and exacerbate psoriasis symptoms.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Certain medications, such as beta-blockers, lithium, and antimalarial drugs, can trigger or worsen psoriasis.

list.title: Weather:
list.snippet: Cold, dry weather can dry out the skin and worsen symptoms, while warm, sunny weather may offer some relief.

list.title: Alcohol and Smoking:
list.snippet: Excessive alcohol consumption and smoking can also contribute to flare-ups.

list.title: Hormonal Changes:
list.snippet: Hormonal fluctuations, such as during puberty, pregnancy, or menopause, can also affect psoriasis symptoms.
Psoriasis is sometimes associated with other autoimmune diseases like lupus, Crohn's disease, and multiple sclerosis.

text_blocks.snippet: By identifying and managing these triggers, individuals with psoriasis can potentially reduce the frequency and severity of flare-ups. Keeping a symptom diary to track potential triggers, practicing stress-reduction techniques, and maintaining good skin care habits are all helpful strategies.
